correctness.rationale: For every p>=5 the 3 possible common valuations exhaust all target pairs. In unit-unit cells, the discriminant-square root count over p^2 has only 2,p,0 solutions, with the nonunit-product exclusion removing one quadratic-residue class. In valuation-one cells, reduction of yuv=s gives two base roots and p lifts for each, hence 2p; zero cell has p(p-1). Counts sum to p^4 when zeros are included; sum of multiplicities equals |U|^2. Energy follows algebraically, and orthogonality gives the exact Fourier normalization. Finite tests for five primes check every target but are not used as a substitute for general proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge novelty of the complete prime-square target-by-target ordered convolution distribution, with four distinct positive levels and their exact multiplicities. Checked primary texts treat general Fourier restriction bounds (Hickman--Wright), distribution of modular inverses (Humphries), bounded quartic Kloosterman collision counts (Ricotta--Royer), and coordinate rather than geometric pair sums (Bower et al.). Related indexed results treat the finite field of p^2 elements, not the nonreduced ring modulo p^2. Prior exact aggregate finite-field fourth moments cannot determine the new ring multiplicity distribution. An undiscovered earlier full distribution remains a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: Search is not uniqueness proof; exact prime-square Kloosterman fourth-moment identities might be implicit in unlocated literature.

value.rationale: This is the complete natural twofold convolution spectrum of the standard modular inverse curve at the first nonreduced modulus level p^2, not an arbitrary table. The distinct singular valuation-one fibers contribute a 2p intensity, and double-root unit strata contribute p instead of the generic 2. These mechanisms give the exact full-frequency Kloosterman fourth moment and a constant-input Fourier extension quotient 6-3/(p-1), asymptotically double the corresponding prime-field ratio. Exact target-count information is useful beyond a global moment bound; no claim of sharp weighted operator norm is needed.
